conclusion: The S-unit arm has a sound two-line injectivity lemma (fix two base elements a>b of A; x -> (a+x, b+x) injects A minus {a,b} into the solutions of U-W=a-b in positive S-smooth U,W), so g(k) <= 2 + max_d N_S(d), and the implication runs the right way (solution-count bound => g bound => Erdos #126, not the reverse). But the strongest applicable theorem, Evertse's 3*7^{d+2s}, gives g(k) <= 2 + 3*7^{2k+3} ~ 1029*49^k, which is weaker than the 1934 Erdos-Turan 3*2^{k-1} and Erdos-Suranyi 2^k by a factor about 24.5^k. Measurement shows the slack is in the theorem, not the route: at k=7 the quantity Evertse bounds by 7.0e14 has measured value 96, against the elementary ceiling 128.
confidence: High on the lemma and on the arithmetic of the comparison: the lemma is elementary and self-contained, Evertse's and Beukers-Schlickewei's statements were read off the Beukers-Schlickewei paper itself rather than from memory, and the smooth-number counter reproduces Lehmer's published Stormer table exactly for k=1..8. Medium on the claim that three-or-more base elements are strictly worse: the linear-dependence argument is solid, but we did not exhaust nonlinear gadgets. Low on any extrapolation of the measured growth of max_d N_S(d): eight points cannot separate k^3.2 from 1.6^k, and the box-truncated counts are lower bounds only, so nothing in column 4 of the results table is an upper bound on g(k). We did not establish that the lemma is new; given Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman 1986 it may well be in the literature, and we do not claim otherwise.

notes_for_operator: The parent asked for one of three deliverables and gets the third (standard S-unit bounds are quantitatively too weak) with a usable version of the second (the missing lemma is named in RESULTS section 7). The number worth carrying back to the parent is the required improvement: Evertse's base 49 must drop below 2 to beat 1934, and to exp(o(k)) to settle #126, while the best known lower bound on unit-equation solution counts is exp((4+o(1))(s/log s)^{1/2}) and the measured Stormer data looks polynomial. So the route is not refuted, it is starved. If the parent is deciding whether to fund a further S-unit lane, the honest read is that the lane's success condition is an improvement to a 1984 Diophantine theorem that has stood for forty years, which is not a lane this laboratory can open at hunt cost.
